title: Looking back
goals: Talk about the past with was / were: what you were like, where you were, and how you felt.
Talk about what you did, using the simple past of regular (-ed) and irregular (went, had, got) verbs.
Say what you didn't do, using didn't + base verb.
Ask and answer questions about experiences: Did you…? Where did you go? How was it?
Describe your first times (my first day, my first pet) with adjectives like nervous, scared, or embarrassing.
Tell about a trip using expressions with get and go, and change the subject with Anyway.

learn.title: was / were: the past of be
learn.html:
To talk about what things were like or where you were in the past. There are only two forms: was and were.

SubjectAffirmativeNegativeQuestion
I / he / she / itI was nervous.She wasn't happy.Was it fun?
you / we / theyWe were late.They weren't at home.Were you scared?
  • Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't. / Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.
  • With was/were, don't use did: Were you at the party? (not Did you were…?).
  • Time expressions: yesterday, last night, last week, two years ago, in 2019.

watch.wrong: I was 10 years old when I moved here, and I were scared.
watch.right: I was 10 years old when I moved here, and I was scared.

watch.wrong: Did you were at the party?
watch.why: With be, don't use did: invert it to were + subject.
Age is expressed with be: I was 15.

learn.title: Simple past: regular verbs
learn.html:
For actions that were finished in the past. Regular verbs add -ed, and the form is the same for all persons.

RuleExamples
Normal: + -edwatch → watched, visit → visited, walk → walked
Ends in -e: + -dlive → lived, like → liked, move → moved
Consonant + y: y → -iedstudy → studied, try → tried
One-syllable CVC: double the last consonantstop → stopped, plan → planned

Negative: didn't (did not) + base verb: I didn't watch TV. The verb goes back to the base form.

Pronunciation of -ed: /t/ (walked), /d/ (lived), and /ɪd/ (visited, wanted).

Time expressions: yesterday, last week, in 2018, three years ago. With ago: I moved here five years ago.

watch.why: After didn't, the verb goes in the base form.
The simple past is used for a finished time (in 2015, ago), not since.

watch.wrong: Two years ago, I visit Cancún.
watch.right: Two years ago, I visited Cancún.
watch.why: With ago, the verb goes in the past.

learn.title: Simple past: irregular verbs
learn.html:
Many very common verbs don't end in -ed: you have to learn their past form. They are the same for all persons, and the negative is also didn't + base verb.

BasePastBasePast
bewas / weremakemade
gowentmeetmet
havehadseesaw
getgoteatate
buyboughtcomecame
taketookgivegave
writewroteforgetforgot

I went to Oaxaca last summer. I didn't go to Puebla.

watch.why: After didn't, use the base form.

watch.wrong: We have a great time yesterday.
watch.right: We had a great time yesterday.
watch.why: Yesterday calls for the past: had.

learn.title: Questions in the past
learn.html:
With regular verbs we use did + subject + base verb. With be, invert was / were.

TypeStructureExample
Yes / NoDid + subject + base verbDid you enjoy the trip?
Yes / No with beWas / Were + subjectWere they nervous?
Wh- with didWh- + did + subject + base verbWhere did you go?
Wh- with beWh- + was / were + subjectHow was your vacation?
  • Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
  • Useful questions: What was the weather like? How long were you there? Who did you go with? What did you do?
  • Only did carries the past: Did you go? (not Did you went?).

watch.wrong: Did you went to the party?
watch.right: Did you go to the party?
watch.why: With did, the verb goes in the base form.

watch.right: Where did you go last summer?
watch.why: Did is missing from the question.

watch.wrong: Yes, I went. (a 'Did you enjoy it?')
watch.why: The short answer repeats did, not the verb.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• How was your weekend? / How was your vacation? — asking about a past experience.
  • It was great! / It was awful! — answering with a short opinion.
  • Did you enjoy it? How about you? — answering and turning the question back.
  • Really? / Oh, no! / Wow! — reacting while the other person talks.
  • Anyway, … — changing the subject or ending the conversation: Anyway, how was your trip?
  • I had a great time. / I made a mistake. — common phrases in the past.
  • What was the weather like? How long were you there? Who did you go with? — questions to ask for details about a trip.

write.prompt: Write 60 to 100 words about your first day at school or work: how you felt, what happened, and how the day ended. Starter: My first day at work was …
checklist: Use was / were to describe how you felt (nervous, scared, relaxed…)
At least three verbs in the past (regular and irregular)
A negative sentence with didn't + base verb
A time expression (yesterday, ago, last year…)
Between 60 and 100 words, with a subject in every sentence
write.model: My first day at work was a big day for me. I was very nervous, and my hands were cold. I arrived at the office early, but nobody was there. Later, my new boss showed me my desk. I met my team and they were very friendly. I didn't understand the computer system, so I asked many questions. I had lunch with two coworkers, and we talked a lot. At six o'clock, I went home tired but relaxed. It was a good day.

write.prompt: Write 60 to 100 words about your last vacation or your last weekend: where you went, with whom, what you did, and how it was. Starter: Last weekend I went …
targets: questions and answers in the past
checklist: Where you went and with whom (went, with)
An expression with get or go (got lost, went hiking…)
A final question with Did you…? or How was…?
An opinion with was/were (It was great)
Between 60 and 100 words
write.model: Last weekend I went to Valle de Bravo with my two best friends. We left early on Saturday and got there at ten. First, we got lost in the town, but a nice man helped us. Then we went hiking near the lake and took many photos. In the evening, we ate fish and played cards. On Sunday, we got up late and came back home in the afternoon. Anyway, it was a great weekend. The weather was perfect and the people were kind. Did you go anywhere last weekend?

reading.title: A first day I will never forget
paragraphs: Last Monday was my first day at a new job. I was very nervous. I got up at six o'clock and I took a shower. I didn't eat breakfast because I was too scared to eat. I took the bus to the office and I got there at eight, one hour early!

The office was big and noisy. A woman named Carmen met me at the door. She was young and friendly. She gave me a coffee and showed me my desk. Then I met my co-workers. Some of them were very kind, but my boss, Mr. Salas, was strict. He said, "We start at nine, not at eight." It was a little embarrassing.
At ten o'clock I made a big mistake. I sent an email to the wrong person! Carmen laughed and said, "Don't worry. I did the same thing on my first day." She helped me write another email.

At lunch, we went to a small restaurant with the team and I had tacos. Everybody was relaxed there, and I felt better. In the afternoon, I learned a lot about the company. I got home at six, tired but happy. My first day wasn't perfect, but it wasn't bad. I was proud of myself.

listening.title: How was your vacation?
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hi, Pete! You're back! When did you get back?
Hi, Karen. I got back on Saturday.
How was your vacation? Where did you go?
It was great! I went to Oaxaca with my sister.
Oh, nice. How long were you there?
We were there for ten days. The weather was hot and sunny.
We went hiking in the mountains, and we visited some old ruins. I also got a bad sunburn!
Ouch! Did you have any problems?
Only one. We got lost on the first day, but a friendly man helped us.
That sounds like fun! Did you eat any good food?
Yes, we did. We ate tlayudas every day. Anyway, how was your weekend?
It was quiet. I stayed home and relaxed.
